neighbours.label: a noun naming a body or physical measurement, or the tool used for it (height, waist size, measuring tape, thermometer, scale)
fire: The nurse wrote down the child's height on the growth chart.
To find your size, wrap a tape measure around your chest.
The doctor checked his temperature with a digital thermometer.
Shoe size depends mostly on the length of your foot.
Step on the bathroom scale each morning before breakfast.
Body mass index is worked out from your weight and height.
Measure your waist circumference just above the hip bones.
A ruler and a level are all you need to hang the shelf straight.
quiet: The nurse wrote down the child's name on the patient chart.
To find your seat, look at the number printed on your ticket.
The doctor checked his throat with a small flashlight.
Shoe style depends mostly on the fashion of the season.
Step into the bathroom each morning before breakfast.
Body mass is mostly made of water, muscle and bone.
Wear your belt just above the hip bones for comfort.
A hammer and some nails are all you need to hang the shelf.
